units.title: Domain B: Evolution and Diversity of Life

outcomes.text: Explain how variation and selection pressure drive evolution.
Discuss biogeographical evidence for evolution.
Analyse molecular-biology evidence for evolution.
Tell convergent from divergent evolution using homologous and analogous structures.
Describe the endosymbiotic theory of how eukaryotes arose from prokaryotes.
Describe Lamarck's inheritance of acquired characters, with the giraffe neck example.
State the weaknesses of Lamarckism.
Describe bryophytes as non-vascular plants.
Explain the life cycle of Polytrichum moss.
Describe the general features of vascular plants.
Identify the divisions of vascular plants.
Explain the general characteristics of pteridophytes.
Explain the life cycle of ferns.
Describe the general characteristics of gymnosperms.
Describe the life cycle of pine.
Describe the general characteristics of angiosperms.
Explain the life cycle of angiosperms.
Describe general characteristics of angiosperm groups and their economic importance.
Identify the two major divisions of animals.
Describe features and importance of invertebrate phyla such as roundworms, molluscs, annelids, arthropods and echinoderms.
Describe the general characteristics of chordates.
Describe the general characteristics of amphibians and other vertebrate classes.
Define biochemistry and molecular biology.
Describe briefly the types of chemical bonds in biological molecules.
State the properties of water that make it the medium of life.
Distinguish carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.
Describe and sketch condensation and hydrolysis reactions.
Define carbohydrates and classify them.
Compare properties and roles of monosaccharides.
Compare isomers and stereoisomers of glucose.
Distinguish properties and roles of disaccharides.
Describe glycosidic bonds in disaccharides.
Describe structure, properties and roles of polysaccharides.
Define proteins and amino acids, and recognise essential amino acids.
Outline how peptide bonds form and break.
Justify why amino acid sequence matters.
Classify proteins as globular or fibrous.
List roles of structural and functional proteins.
Define lipids.
Describe properties and roles of acylglycerols, waxes and phospholipids.
Illustrate the molecular structure of fats and phospholipids.
Evaluate steroids and prostaglandins as important lipids.
Describe nucleic acids and the molecular structure of nucleotides.
Distinguish the nitrogenous bases in nucleic acids.
Outline mononucleotide examples such as ATP.
Illustrate formation of the phosphodiester bond.
Explain the double helix structure of DNA.
Explain the general structure of RNA.
Distinguish the types of RNA by function.
Discuss the central dogma.
Define conjugated molecules and describe roles of glycoproteins, lipoproteins and nucleoproteins.
Describe cells as the basic unit of life.
Differentiate prokaryotic from eukaryotic cells.
State cell theory and how it was tested.
Identify the ultrastructure of animal and plant cells.
Describe structure and function of subcellular organelles.
Compare and contrast light and electron microscopes.
Define cell signalling.
Discuss the path of a signal from outside the cell to a response.
Define stem cells and the benefits of using them.
Categorise the types of stem cells.
Evaluate advantages and disadvantages of stem cell use.
Explain the structure of the cell membrane and its parts.
Write the chemical structure of a phospholipid with saturated and unsaturated tails.
Explain the four membrane transport mechanisms with examples.
Describe endocytosis and exocytosis with examples.
Compare simple and facilitated diffusion.
Explain the steps of mitosis and meiosis with diagrams.
Identify the role and parts of the enzyme active site.
Differentiate the three types of cofactors.
Explain enzyme action through the lock-and-key and induced-fit models.
Explain enzyme catalysis using a specific example.
Define activation energy and show how enzymes lower it.
Explain the effect of temperature on enzyme reaction rate.
Investigate how pH affects enzyme activity, for example papain.
Show that enzyme concentration affects reaction rate.
Describe enzyme inhibition, its types and importance.
Name molecules that act as inhibitors.
Categorise inhibitors as competitive or non-competitive.
Explain feedback inhibition.
Classify enzymes by the reactions they catalyse.
Classify enzymes by the substrates they act on.
Explain the roles of light, carbon dioxide and water in photosynthesis.
Identify the two kinds of photosynthetic pigments.
Describe the roles of photosynthetic pigments.
Differentiate absorption spectra from action spectra.
Describe the arrangement of photosystems in the thylakoid.
Describe the events of non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
Explain the Calvin cycle and regeneration of RuBP.
Justify the importance of G3P in photosynthesis.
Define photorespiration.
Outline the events of photorespiration.
Rationalise how a wasteful process like photorespiration persists.
Outline C4 photosynthesis as an adaptation.
Explain anaerobic respiration in yeast and muscle, producing ethanol or lactate.
Explain substrate-level phosphorylation in glycolysis and the Krebs cycle.
Illustrate the link reaction converting pyruvate to acetyl CoA.
Outline the steps of the Krebs cycle.
Trace electrons through the electron transport chain.
Describe chemiosmosis and relate it to electron transport.
Explain how temperature affects oxidative phosphorylation.
Outline how acetyl CoA forms from fats.
Compare respiration of fats and carbohydrates.
Describe the structures of the male reproductive system.
Define male reproductive hormones and explain their roles.
Explain the structures of the female reproductive system.
Describe the menstrual cycle and the hormones controlling it.
Define a gene as a nucleotide sequence within DNA.
Explain the laws of segregation and independent assortment.
Relate independent assortment to dihybrid crosses.
Express limits of independent assortment.
Show that independent assortment creates variation.
Evaluate how gene inheritance and mixing create variety.
Describe exceptions to Mendel's laws.
Explain incomplete dominance with an example.
Differentiate incomplete dominance from codominance.

subtopics.title: Multiple alleles and ABO blood groups

outcomes.text: Define alleles and multiple alleles.
State the alleles behind ABO blood groups.
Explain codominance when two alleles are equally expressed.
Name the human blood group systems.
Investigate why O-negative people are universal donors.
Describe some other blood group systems.
Associate positive and negative blood groups with the Rh factor.
Justify why Rh incompatibility endangers a baby.
Explain erythroblastosis fetalis using Rh genetics.
Suggest measures to prevent Rh problems.
Define and relate polygenic inheritance and epistasis.
Describe polygenic inheritance using plant and animal examples.
List at least five polygenic traits found in humans.
Give epistasis examples from mammals and plants.
Describe gene linkage and crossing over.
Explain how linkage counters independent assortment.
Suggest how linkage can be observed or evaluated.
Explain the XX-XY mechanism of sex determination.
Identify males and females from karyotypes.
Solve genetics problems on XX-XY sex determination.
Describe the concept of sex linkage.
Explain inheritance of sex-linked traits such as eye colour.
Describe sex-linked inheritance in males and females.
Describe X-linked disorders and their inheritance patterns.
Name some human sex-linked disorders.

subtopics.title: Chromosomes and DNA as genetic material

outcomes.text: Explain techniques used for embryonic sex and genetic screening.
Annotate the detailed structure of a chromosome.
Narrate Griffith and Avery's experiments on genetic material.
Describe the three proposed models of DNA replication.
Narrate Meselson and Stahl's experiment supporting semi-conservative replication.
Describe the events of DNA replication.
Describe DNA stability and variability.
Describe characteristics of the genetic code.
Differentiate genetic code from codon and anticodon terms.
Explain the mechanism of transcription.
Explain why mRNA length differs from gene length.
Describe the mechanism of protein synthesis.
State differences between protein synthesis in prokaryotes and eukaryotes.
Suggest ways the synthesised protein is processed and targeted.
State the importance of regulating gene expression.
Describe negative control of gene expression.
Describe positive control of gene expression.
Define mutation and identify its sources.
Differentiate natural from induced mutations.
Justify why most mutations are harmful.
Rationalise that some mutations may aid evolution.
Describe symptoms, causes and treatments of chromosomal mutations such as Down syndrome.
Describe symptoms, causes and treatments of some gene mutations.
Define species, population, community and ecosystem.
Distinguish the modes of nutrition.
Identify plants as producers that convert light energy to chemical energy.
Define trophic levels.
Discuss energy loss between trophic levels.
Describe gross and net primary productivity.
Interpret pyramids of number, biomass and energy.
Explain the greenhouse effect with examples of gases.
Describe the harmful effects of greenhouse gases.
Explain ocean acidification and coral bleaching.
Define biogeochemical cycles and locate their reservoirs.
Describe the water cycle in detail.
Define aquifers and water table.
Discuss the nitrogen cycle in detail.
Define ecological succession.
Describe primary and secondary succession.
Differentiate xerarch from hydrarch succession.
Explain xerarch succession on bare rock up to flowering plants.
Describe characteristics of a population such as growth and density.
Explain the effects of human population growth.
Describe the four important ecosystems of Pakistan.

units.title: Domain O: Prokaryotes, Protists and Fungi

outcomes.text: Outline the taxonomic position of prokaryotes.
Explain the phylogenetic position of prokaryotes.
Justify why bacteria live in the widest range of habitats.
Draw an annotated generalised bacterial cell.
Justify why cyanobacteria are considered the most successful prokaryotes.
Describe the structure and chemistry of the bacterial cell wall.
Compare cell walls of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
Illustrate the variety of bacterial shapes with diagrams.
Justify endospore formation as a survival strategy.
Explain motility in bacteria.
Describe bacterial flagella and other appendages with diagrams.
Describe genomic organisation of bacteria.
Classify bacteria by their methods of nutrition.
Differentiate bacterial photosynthesis from plant photosynthesis.
List the phases of bacterial growth.
Describe methods of bacterial reproduction.
Describe bacteria as recyclers of nature.
Explain the use of bacteria in research and industry.
Describe important bacterial diseases in humans.
Describe important bacterial diseases in plants.
Define normal flora.
Describe benefits of human bacterial flora.
List chemical and physical methods to control bacteria.
Explain protists as a diverse group of eukaryotes.
Describe salient features and examples of protist groups.
Justify why protists matter to humans.
Classify fungi into zygomycota, ascomycota and basidiomycota.
Explain yeast as a unicellular fungus used by humans.
Name fungi that yield antibiotics.
Explain mutualism in mycorrhizae.
Give examples of edible fungi.
Describe the ecological impact of fungi that cause plant disease.
Discuss the pathogenic role of fungi.
Justify the status of viruses between living and non-living.
Trace the history of viruses since discovery.
Classify viruses by host and structure.
Describe the structure of a model bacteriophage.
Justify that a virus needs a host cell to reproduce.
Explain how a virus survives protected inside a host cell.
Determine the method a virus uses to complete its life cycle.
Describe lytic and lysogenic life cycles of a bacteriophage.
Outline uses of bacteriophages in genetic engineering.
Explain the life cycle of HIV.
Justify the name Human Immunodeficiency Virus.
Reason out HIV specificity for its host cells.
List the symptoms of AIDS.
Explain opportunistic diseases that strike AIDS patients.
Describe treatments available for AIDS.
List common measures to control the spread of viral disease.

subtopics.title: Other viral diseases, prions and viroids

outcomes.text: Describe cause, symptoms, treatment and prevention of common viral diseases.
List the transmission sources of each viral disease.
Describe the structure of prions and viroids.
List diseases caused by prions and viroids.
Interpret how viral infections cause global economic loss.
Describe limitations of vaccines against viral disease.
List macro and micronutrients of plants.
State examples of carnivorous plants.
Explain the role of stomata and palisade tissue in gas exchange.
Relate transpiration to gas exchange in plants.
Describe how stomata open and close.
Assess the structure of xylem vessels and sieve tubes with their functions.
Discuss water movement between plant cells.
Describe water movement through roots.
Explain water movement in xylem.
Explain the movement of sugars in plants.
Define osmotic adjustment.
State water movement into or out of cells in different solutions.
Explain osmotic adjustment in hydrophytes, mesophytes and xerophytes.
List plant adaptations to low and high water availability.
Explain turgor pressure and its importance.
Describe the structure of supporting tissues in plants.
Define growth and explain primary and secondary growth.
Justify the formation of annual rings.
Explain the influence of apical meristem on plant growth.
Outline the roles of important plant growth regulators.
Explain the types of movement in plants.
Define photoperiodism.
Classify plants by flowering response to day length.
Explain the role of low-temperature treatment on flowering.
Make decisions about measurements and observations in an investigation.
Choose and control variables in an investigation.
Plan a procedure that gives reliable data.
Record data and observations clearly in tables.
Display calculations and reasoning properly.
Make and use observations with a light microscope and photomicrographs.
Draw and label specimens in an investigation.
Calibrate and measure using microscope scales.
Interpret data and observations.
Draw conclusions from investigation results.
Use results and information to reach supported conclusions.
Identify sources of error and suggest improvements.
